_comment: First-person animations. Edit, then press F3+T in-game to reload. Values are for the right hand; the left hand mirrors automatically. translation is applied after vanilla's arm transform (x right, y up, z toward the camera, so negative z pushes forward); rotation is degrees around X, then Y, then Z. Held poses use blend_in_ticks / blend_out_ticks. One-shot effects use translation/rotation as their peak and duration_ticks as their length. tremble shakes the pose as a charge fills; ready_pop pushes along Z once it's full.
_model_roll: model_roll (trident_lowered, jab_spear): degrees the trident turns around its own pole while the pose plays, blended in with it. 90 fans the prongs flat across the view; use -90 for the other face, 0 to turn it off.
_dagger_throw: Right-click throw wind-up (first person), once the dagger is caught; the ready hold itself is dagger_throw_flip's last key. keys: one key (translation / rotation / orient as in dagger_throw_flip) added on top of the hold, eased in over blend_in_ticks; tremble shakes it meanwhile.
_dagger_throw_flip: Readying a dagger throw: a short dip, then tossed up edge first, tumbling forward end over end for a half turn, caught by the blade with the handle up and forward. duration_ticks is its length (the throw is ready after 7 ticks); the last key (t 1.0) is the ready hold, kept until the throw. First person, per key at progress t: translation is the dagger's center from vanilla's first-person hand anchor (x right, y up, z toward the camera); rotation is [pitch, yaw, roll] from facing the camera flat with the blade straight up: pitch turns about the screen X axis, so it is the forward tumble (negative tips the point away from you; give the airborne keys a steady step for a steady spin), roll leans it in the screen plane; orient is applied after, in the blade's own frame: orient Y turns it about its length (about -80 to -100 leaves it 60-70 degrees from flat, edge first). Every key needs orient. Rest before the first key is vanilla's hold: [0.0706, 0.2, 0.0706], rotation [20, 0, 0], orient [0, -90, 0]. The left hand mirrors. Screen check: the hand camera has a 70 degree FOV and the anchor sits at about (0.56, -0.52, -0.72), so keep y / -z under ~0.7 and x / -z under ~1.2. Third person spins the dagger in its own plane by the keys' pitch, scaled so it ends at a half turn (-180).
_swings: Attack swings below only apply without Better Combat. duration_ticks also sets the arm swing length (vanilla is 6).
_jab_spear: Spears and tridents poke like vanilla 26.x's spear STAB; duration_ticks is the swing length. For tridents only, translation/rotation are an extra offset (screen space, applied before the STAB) held while the trident is out, following the STAB's own thrust curve; model_roll rolls it around its pole the same way.
_heavy_longsword: Longsword swing (without Better Combat): a horizontal cut, right to left, then the left-to-right return cut on the next swing (heavy_longsword_back; it uses heavy_longsword's duration). The blade turns round the grip like a clock hand while the hand sweeps across the view at crosshair height: in from off-screen right, through the middle of the screen (the t 0.45 key puts the grip just below the crosshair with the blade pitched up through it), out off-screen left. Translation y +0.63 lifts the grip from about 0.71 below eye level to about 0.08 below. In third person the swing plays 1.5x as long as here (CombatClientPoses.THIRD_PERSON_SWING_STRETCH). rotation (on the entry) is the idle hold's blade heading and pivot the grip, both relative to vanilla's first-person hand: leave them unless the in-hand model changes. keys: at swing progress t (0..1), translation moves the hand from the idle hold (x right, y up, z toward the camera) and rotation is the blade's heading [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees (yaw 0 = straight ahead, +90 = left; pitch raises the tip; roll twists the flat, 0 = flat facing up). Each key is eased in from the previous one (ease: linear, in, out, inout, in_cubic, out_cubic); the motion starts from and settles back to the idle hold. longsword_spin uses the same format (it plays with Better Combat too).

third_person._comment: Arm angles in degrees on the player model (X pitch: negative raises the arm forward/up; Y yaw: negative turns the right arm inward). Written for a right-handed player: main_arm is the right arm, off_arm the left (positive Y turns it inward). Mirrored for left-handers. off_arm only applies with an empty offhand, except shield_bash, where it is the arm holding the shield. item turns the held item: [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees, roll twisting it around the arm's length. Blending uses the timings above.
third_person._longsword_grip: Idle two-handed hold between swings (no Better Combat): the sword arm is set outright, so walking does not swing it (walk_bob is ignored here; crouching still leans the grip with the torso). item turns the sword in the fist (pitch tips the blade up or down, roll twists it around the forearm); longsword item turns pivot on the fist's centre, so the hilt stays in the hand. The off arm is not keyed: it is solved every frame (CombatThirdPerson.offHandOnHilt) so its hand grips the hilt about 3px below the sword hand, so off_arm is ignored for the grip and the swings. Model arms are straight, so both hands can only meet roughly in front of the chest: if you move main_arm far out to the side, the off hand will come up short of the hilt.
third_person._heavy_longsword: Swing and spin keys: at progress t, main_arm angles (relative to the torso), body = upper-body twist in degrees (positive turns toward the off hand, so the cut carries the torso round), item = [pitch, yaw, roll] turn of the held sword (roll twists it around the forearm; with roll near 90 the blade lies flat and pitch swings it round in the cut). Eased like the first-person keys; before the first key and after the last the arms blend with the grip. The swing's item turns are interpolated along the shortest rotation between keys. heavy_longsword: wound up with the blade back over the sword arm's shoulder (t 0.18), cut right to left at chest height (0.36 to 0.6), follow-through with the blade back past the off side (0.72). heavy_longsword_back is the return cut, left to right. off_arm is ignored here (the off hand follows the hilt); longsword_spin still uses its off_arm keys.
third_person._longsword_spin: Right-click spin (plays with Better Combat too): longsword_spin_charge is the hold while charging, the two-handed wind-up with the blade drawn back over the sword arm's shoulder and the torso turned toward it; its one key (t is ignored) gives main_arm, body twist and item like the swing keys, and main_arm outside the key is the one-handed fallback when the offhand is in use. longsword_spin keys work like heavy_longsword's: the wind-up (t 0.12, matching the charge), the cut held out level at chest height while the whole body turns 360 degrees (t 0.12 to 0.85, LongswordSpinClient.bodySpin; right-handers turn left), a follow-through, then back to the grip. off_arm is ignored for both: with an empty offhand the off hand is put on the hilt.
